judge_assessment.explanation: The verdict is right and I confirmed every result against the tikz grids rather than the prose: problem 2's rectangle is a 4x3 grid cut at x=1, so 3 and 9 squares (3 < 9); problem 3's is a 6x2 grid cut at x=2, so 4 and 8 with 12 total, making the correct transfer (4+8)/2 - 4 = 2 squares; problem 4's 4x4 grid cut at x=2 with horizontal cuts at y=3 (left) and y=1 (right) gives pieces of 2, 6, 6, 2; problem 5's grid is 5x4 = 20 squares, so 20/4 = 5. One judge number is wrong: 'Verified equal 3-and-3 halves' for problem 1. That figure is a 4x3 grid cut at x=2, so each part holds SIX squares; verify.json id 1 is {'values': [6, 6], 'expected': '='} and the answer key reasons '6 = 6'. The relation is right, the count is not. The judge also did not open the Quick Answers bank, which prints '1. -' and '2. -' for the two verified relations ('=' and '<') using the same glyph as row 6, the one genuinely manual item -- so on a six-problem sheet a grader sees three dashes and can tell only from the body which were checked. Finally, problem 2 ends 'Then tell a friend why Part A is not one half', an explanation with no manual entry, on a prompt that explicitly asked to label genuinely open responses.

strengths_to_preserve: The two misconception traps are computed rather than asserted: verify.json declares {'expr': 'b - a', 'value': 4} for Ben's 'move 4 squares' and {'expr': 't/2', 'value': 10} for Ivy's fold-once error, so the planted wrong result is machine-proved distinct from the right one -- exactly what the prompt's 'declare any planted wrong results as machine-checked misconception traps' asked for.

Every count stated in prose is realised in the drawing: problem 2 says 3 and 9 squares and the tikz cuts a 4x3 grid at x=1 to produce precisely that, so a child who counts and a child who reads get the same numbers.

Problem 3 is the sharpest item -- Ben's error is not 'wrong arithmetic' but a plausible strategy (move the whole difference) that merely swaps which part is bigger, which is a genuine equal-shares misconception rather than a slip.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt passes relation strings to bare sympy.sympify, which raises, and returns '---' -- the same string render_entry emits for a manual-only problem. Two verified relations and one genuine manual item print identically.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '1. -  2. -  ... 6. -' with only rows 3, 4, 5 carrying values.
verify.json id 1 is compare '=' (verified), id 2 is compare '<' (verified), id 6 is the only manual entry.

root_causes.description: An item can demand a written explanation and still be recorded as fully machine-verified, because no gate ties explanation prose to a manual entry. Problem 2 asks the child to say why Part A is not one half and carries only a compare entry, while problem 6's explanation is correctly flagged -- the sheet is internally inconsistent about the same demand.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 2: 'Write $=$, $<$, or $>$ between the two counts to show what is really true. Then tell a friend why Part A is not one half.'
verify.json id 2 has a single compare entry; no manual entry exists for id 2.
verify.json id 6 IS manual for a drawing plus explanation, so the author knew the pattern.
The task prompt required 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'.

improvements.title: Render the verified '=' and '<' in the Quick Answers bank instead of a manual dash
improvements.proposed_change: Handle relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=') in scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt before the sympify call and typeset them with the entry's compared 'values' (e.g. '$6 = 6$', '$3 < 9$'), and emit a distinct marker for manual-only rows so row 6 no longer looks identical to rows 1 and 2.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: render_entry on {'type': 'compare', 'values': [6, 6], 'order': 'relation', 'expected': '='} must return the relation, not '---', and must differ from the manual-only marker. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Half the rows of this six-row bank regain content, and the equal-shares sheet's central answers ('the parts ARE equal', 'they are NOT equal') become checkable at a glance.
improvements.risk: Slightly wider bank entries can shift the adaptive column count; re-check the answer-key page budget.

improvements.title: Give problem 2's 'tell a friend why' its own manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate that scans each \problem body for explanation cues ('tell a friend', 'tell your grown-up', 'explain', 'why', 'how you know') and fails the build unless that problem id carries a manual entry alongside its machine checks. SKILL.md already reserves manual for explanation answers; make it mechanical rather than advisory, and have the delivery summary derive its manual count from verify.json instead of prose.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem text contains 'Then tell a friend why ...' with only a compare entry: the gate exits non-zero; adding a manual entry for that id makes it pass. Fails today (curr-049 built green with exactly that shape).
improvements.expected_impact: The adult grading a misconception sheet is told which explanations need reading, which is the whole point of an error-analysis format.
improvements.risk: Cue-word scanning can misfire on narrative prose inside a problem stem; restrict it to imperative sentences in \problem bodies and allow an explicit author override.

case_summary: A mathematically sound equal-shares packet whose figures and prose agree square for square -- I recounted all five grids from the tikz and every count, ordering and repair value in verify.json is correct, including the (4+8)/2 - 4 = 2 transfer and 20/4 = 5. It meets the prompt's specific demands: three find-and-fix items (more than the two required) and two machine-computed misconception traps. Two defects survive the 32/32: the Quick Answers bank prints dashes for the two verified relations, indistinguishable from the genuine manual row, and problem 2's 'tell a friend why' explanation is unflagged on a prompt that explicitly required open responses to be labelled. The judge's '3-and-3 halves' for problem 1 misstates a figure that holds 6 squares per part.
